what: Every pull request now runs all the automated checks on GitHub, in a job named checks, at both window sizes; drafts too.
The pull request's run summary says when the pull request changes a file that judges it, or removes tests. It never fails the run.
The hand-over page counts and names each browser test that failed when run with the others and passed when run alone.
The unit tests now go red after 3 minutes and the browser tests after 8, about three times a normal run.
A quick run, python3 checks.py --quick, tests the pages at one window size; the page never counts it as a full run.
so_what: You can merge on a result from a machine the building agent cannot touch, once you require the checks job on main.
Try first: open this build's pull request and watch the checks run on GitHub; it is the first run the new workflow makes.
A green result with a wobble in it is now shown to you on this page instead of passing quietly.
A hung or much slower check now turns red instead of passing.
From the next build, the runs in the middle of a build are quick runs and take about a minute less each.
now_what: The skill file is now edited as ticket 10 asked: you allowed it after the build, when the session had been refused the edit. skill-edits.md records the changes.
First run on GitHub, step 1: accept the build and open the pull request.
Step 2: watch the checks run on the pull request and note how long it takes; then tighten its 20-minute limit to fit.
Step 3: on GitHub, protect main: require the checks status check, apply it to administrators, allow no direct push.
Step 4: merge. Later, a rehearsal with a test broken on purpose confirms that a red pull request is refused.
Nothing here shows the workflow works on GitHub: GitHub cannot be run from this machine. The automated checks only read the workflow's text.
A pull request runs its own branch's copy of the workflow, not main's (GitHub's 'Events that trigger workflows', pull_request). Ticket 03's comments link it.
So a pull request can change or silence the notice in the same run that should report it: the notice is for you to read, not a guard.
I ran both on the last code: a full run took 3.7 minutes (unit 1.1, browser tests 2.5) and a quick run 2.5 (unit 1.1, browser tests 1.4).
The recording has nothing to show: no app page changed. The page counts tests of the browser-test runner as browser tests, because they sit in the same folder.
Defaults used, none confirmed by you: GitHub limit 20 minutes; a flaky browser test is shown, not red; limits 3 and 8 minutes; ubuntu-latest; Python 3.13; --quick.
The brief was wrong in one place: the GitHub job installs the WebKit browser as well as Chromium, because the acceptance test runs in WebKit and is part of the checks.
The brief's 'give it a fifteen-minute timeout' does not fit: the agent's command tool waits ten minutes at most. The notes now say to run a whole run in the background.
The first browser-test run now stops at 20 failures, so a mass failure names its tests inside the 8-minute limit. The re-runs are unchanged.
A flaky browser test does not turn the run red; to change that, set FLAKY_IS_RED to True in the browser-test runner, one line.

walk_through.title: No app page changed, so this recording has nothing to show
walk_through.legend: This test checks the browser-test runner itself, with stand-in runs; it opens no browser. Expect an empty or missing recording. What the build changed is judged from the automated checks and the review on this page.
